objectDesc.p: Palm-leaf manuscript. 80 leaves in Javanese script of the Merapi-Merbabu type. The top and bottom lines of the leaves are darkened and often illegible. The leaves have no original numbering (or it is illegible) and seem to be out of order. The most frequently encountered feature in this manuscript is that nasal sound marks, such as ṁ and n, at the end of words are often ignored by the scribe. In addition, vowels or consonants at the end of a word are sometimes linked to the following word. Meanwhile, diphthong sounds such as "ai" replacing "e" and "au" for "o" tend to be commonly found. Uniquely, the number 8 in this ms. is sometimes written like "pha"—possibly due to the phonetic similarity between the aksara "pha" and "pa", whereas "pa" is more naturally used when writing the number 8.

handNote.p: main hand of the manuscript, black ink, Javanese script

history.p: Purchased from B. Farrer, 1888. The manuscript was copied in the hermitage of "Pasanten", located on the western slope of Mount Damalung (nowaday Merbabu), in the Śaka 1557, i.e., 1635 AD
